svg.title: Tropo crew topology — one agent, one clone, main is the bus. Seven working trees against one origin; reference clones borrow the primary's object store; .tropo/flags/resident.json decides which folder an agent boots in; the rule is Mike-locked provisionally and its review condition is unsatisfied.
svg.text: Crew topology — one agent, one clone, main is the bus
Seven working trees on one laptop, one origin. `.tropo/WAKE-DISCIPLINE.md` (uid d2bb4dda), clone clause added v1.2.0 on 2026-09-03.
origin/main — the only meeting point
origin = mike-tropo/argo-os.git · there is no per-agent branch
All seven trees sit on main — git refuses two worktrees on one
branch, so only a clone lets every agent sit literally on main.
emit — write event · commit vault/events/ · git push origin main
BY HAND: the tool does not push — see below
drain — git fetch origin · integrate origin/main · then read
BY HAND: the tool does not fetch — see below
main is the bus
argo-os/ — primary checkout
the one folder the founder opens
resident: talos · T65
.git/objects 560M — lends to clones
refreshes when its resident fetches
.crew/argus/
resident: argus · A175
own .git/config + index
.git 19M · borrows
.crew/argus-a174/
resident: argus · A174
own .git/config + index
.git 525M · no borrow
.crew/metis/
resident: metis · G126
own .git/config + index
.git 116M · borrows
.crew/orpheus/
resident: orpheus · O39
own .git/config + index
.git 29M · borrows
.crew/talos/
no resident marker
own .git/config + index
.git 22M · borrows
.crew/vela/
no resident marker
own .git/config + index
.git 42M · borrows
git clone --reference <primary> — the clone's .git/objects/info/alternates points at argo-os/.git/objects (playbook 99341618.md:180)
5 of 6 borrow and pay only a working tree (.git 19M–116M). .crew/argus-a174/ has no alternates file and pays the full 525M — the cost of independence, and the control on the claim.
Which tree does an agent boot in? — .tropo/flags/resident.json
RULED · NO TOOL
absent · or names a generation with both born and retired → FREE: claim it, boot HERE
a born with NO retired for the NAMED generation → OCCUPIED: boot in .crew/<slug>/
lineage unreadable → OCCUPIED anyway: a wrong "free" puts two agents in one tree
Reads the generation the marker NAMES, never the file's last line (playbook 99341618.md:178).
Prose only — no tool writes this marker, and none evaluates the born/retired test.
Also .tropo/boot-fast-path.md:67. Gitignored (.gitignore:181): a per-tree fact that never travels.
One declared shape. Nothing validates it. — measured 2026-09-08
{agent, generation, since} — argo-os/ · .crew/argus/ · .crew/metis/ (declared)
+ a reason field — .crew/argus-a174/
at / root instead of since — .crew/orpheus/
no marker at all — .crew/talos/ · .crew/vela/
Five markers live across seven trees, in three shapes. The playbook declares one shape.
The marker is what decides the folder, and nothing checks that it is well-formed.
Once falsified — 2026-09-07: generations A173 and A174 both worked .crew/argus/, and one rebased and pushed the other's commit.

It keys on the AGENT, not the session — two generations of one agent still share a tree. The .crew/argus-a174/ clone is the local cure; task f0152d3d8326 closed same day, but the general boot-router fix is unbuilt.
Clause 4 says the tools carry the protocol. They do not.
tropo-emit-event.py — 790 lines, zero occurrences of "git push"
tropo-check-events.py — 829 lines, zero occurrences of "git fetch"
subprocess is imported by the emit tool and never called
task f0151812d521 · assigned to talos · status: new since 2026-09-03
Until it lands, every agent does both halves of the bus by hand and the rule holds only as discipline.
PROVISIONAL LOCK — the review condition is unsatisfied
Mike, 2026-09-03: "I will lock it, but on a provisional basis... I lock it."
Condition: binding now, reviewed after v1.94 fires (WAKE-DISCIPLINE.md:17, :139)
v1.94 never fired — f015fd0f0dee: status pre-ship, publish_state deferred-by-mike
v1.95.0 shipped instead, public 2026-09-07T11:32:58Z — the condition did not clear
The lock has been binding, and unreviewed, since 2026-09-03.
navy / steel — BUILT and in routine use
amber — ruled but unbuilt, unproven, or held
red — known broken, or an unlanded cure
green (proven) — unused here: nothing has earned it
One agent, one clone; emit pushes, drain fetches. The layout is built and measured; the protocol that keeps it honest is still a habit.
